messages.text: Buenos dias, Irene. Are you stopping at the community center before coffee or after?
Before, if my knee behaves. I have my little paper already penciled and folded in the purse.
Good. I saved the Chronicle clipping from yesterday in case you still wanted to compare the last two names.
Bring it, please. Father Miguel's group talked about one of those too, but I want to look one more time.
Buenos dias, Irene. Is Thursday still good for La Madeleine? I can get there by 10:15.
Yes, 10:15 is good. Same little table by the window if it is open.
Perfect. Just us, then. I will bring the picture from the old classroom.
That sounds right. I am keeping the rest of that day plain.
I saw the packet you left in the lounge. The Spanish-English picture cards were neat, Irene.
Room 4 kept losing time after circle, so I added the little hand signs and the clean-up song order.
That part about calling home before the folder note was very you.
If the grown-ups hear a steady voice first, the child hears one too.
Did you do your little walk before the heat, hermana?
Yes, two blocks, then rosary and three lines in the notebook. I still came back to look at the back door twice.
One thing at a time. Put the kettle on, sit with the knitting, and call me after breakfast if your head keeps circling.
I will. Also checking the 10:30 clinic time before I leave, so I don't keep opening the calendar.
Did you eat, Irene? You sounded tight on the phone Sunday.
Beans and rice, yes. That envelope from CenterPoint got me worked up again.
Call me after dishes. One thing at a time.
I will. I don't want to put that mess where everybody can see it.
Ma you need me to drive you by the county place before my first call?
No mijo, Ana is taking me at 8. I wrote my choices last night so I won't stand there reading everything.
Ok Ma. Take the blue card and your glasses.
Already in the bag with that thick booklet from the library table.
Ok Ma, I can stop by Thursday after work and listen to the outside unit. Don't agree to the first quote yet.
Ma, Ana says the family worksheet asks what Abuelo did. Should I put the part about patching roofs and fixing apartment hallways?
Gracias. The man said the capacitor may be $285 if that is all. I moved $40 over this morning and don't want to pull from the little back-up account unless I must.
Yes, mijo. He always came home with paint on his hands and cement dust on his shoes.
Let me check it first. Filters are cheaper than guessing.
And for Abuela, the machine by the kitchen window plus the house keys from those ladies?
That sounds right. Leave my own boxes blank where it asks about campus papers or uniform papers.
Ok Ma, the tire place said the back two can't wait much longer. I can go with you Saturday morning.
Good. March already has the house policy draft and the clinic bill, so I am trying to keep every dollar in its place.
Saturday is fine. I can handle the smaller one now, but if they say all four I need them to split it.
Ask for the written estimate first. Same like with the hallway leak, don't let them add everything at once.
Yes. The card already has the mouth work and the kitchen faucet on it, so I am watching every dollar.
Mija, when you get a minute at work, can you look at the screenshot I sent? It says blood pressure drops fast with one kitchen drink.
I saw it. The page is mostly a sales button and the headline is doing too much.
That is what bothered me. So many big letters and marks at the end.
Wait for your clinic handout. I will send you a plain page from the hospital site at lunch.
Mom, are you still going to that Saturday thing downtown or just sending something?
Too many people for me, mija. I did the $12 online and wrote Mrs. Nguyen about her book basket.
That sounds more your speed. Which books?
The ones where the little boys can point and say, that one looks like me. I keep thinking of those classroom shelves.
Good morning, Irene. I found my old handout for the 3-year-olds: greeting, picture cards, then the song basket. Do you still want it for your notes?
Yes, please. I am putting the songs next to the little story about El Cipitio so a new teacher can see how to do circle time.
I remember how quiet they got when you used the shawl and the little drum. Send me one page and I will mark it before coffee.
I will bring two pages Friday, one for the story basket and one for asking grandparents what song they remember.
Buenos dias, Irene. For coffee Friday, bring that little folder with the 1988 papers if you still want me to look at the dates.
I found it behind my old lesson plan binders. I also found the Saturday training certificates from the same year.
Of course you saved those. That was when you came to school early, stayed late, and still sent notes home in Spanish and English.
Those families needed steady hands. I can bring pupusas too, but no long story at the table, please.
Irene, are you going to that candidate coffee at the library Saturday? They said teachers can ask questions first.
Yes, if my knee behaves. I want to hear who talks plain about pre-K rooms and the clinic on Bissonnet, not just slogans.
Good. Ask them about aides too. These young teachers are drowning.
And I want to see how they treat people in the room. A nice mailer is easy.
Irene, are you still coming for coffee Friday, or did that sour feeling come back?
Still coming. I put the small kettle on and moved my library paperback to the chair, just until my middle settles.
Good. If it keeps on tomorrow, call the office, amiga. No waiting and guessing.
Yes, yes. If it is still there after breakfast I will call. Tonight I only want warm cup, two pages, lights out.
Found that cracked green bowl from Mama's cabinet. Remember how it sat by the little radio?
Yes, by the stove. Papi would turn the dial until the announcer from El Salvador came clear.
And you, me, and the boys trying to get tortillas before Tia moved her sewing things off the table.
That table was never empty in that Bissonnet house.
Ma, the pharmacy on Bellaire sent me a notice too. Are you going there today or waiting?
Waiting until Dr. Patel's nurse calls me back. I want her to look at the list first.
Ok Ma. I can drive you after work if she says yes.
Gracias. I also asked the counter lady to save me the paper they print from the official site.
Hermana, ya llegaste? Vi muchas patrullas en Bissonnet.
Ya en casa. Me pararon en Beechnut por la luz de atras. Solo advertencia gracias a Dios, pero me temblaban las manos todo el camino.
Ay Irene. Tu manejas bien, nunca has tenido problemas con ellos en 70 anos. Respira.
Si, una cosa a la vez. Voy a llamar a Rafael manana para que me cambie el foco.
Mom, Lucia's pickup moved to 3:10 today. Can you do it or are you still at the center?
I am done there at 12:30 on Fridays now. I can eat quick and get her.
Thank you. I saw your tote by the table yesterday, still doing the little papers?
Yes, just the name cards and songs for Monday. Better to finish them at my kitchen table.
Ma, we left Katy late. Lucia has her backpack and sketchbook. Do you still want me to bring the air mattress pump?
Yes mija, bring it please. I made space in the front room after moving my laundry basket.
Ok. I packed her school clothes for Monday so Rafael can take her from your side Sunday night.
Good. I have soup, rice, and the little shampoo she likes.
Irene, did the little ones like the pollito song this morning?
They clapped on pollito and chick, so tomorrow I may use both cards again.
Good. Keep the parents' note simple, querida. Two lines is enough.
Yes, I wrote: painting smock Monday, cuento bag Wednesday, counting lids Friday.
Abuela can I sleep over Saturday? Ana says ask you first.
Abuela, art club has orange paper flowers left over. Do you want some for your picture table?
Yes mija. I put it on the kitchen square already. I also wrote pupusa masa, curtido cabbage, and extra milk on the store paper.
Yes mija, save me a few. The bright ones look nice around your great-grandparents' frames.
Can we make the cheese ones? I have an art club photo to show you.
Also Mom said you were on your feet at the hall again. Sit down this weekend pls.
I will. Sunday I may go just for the morning part and come straight home.
Bring it. Tonight I am writing down what I ate and the old story about your great-grandmother so I do not forget before you come.
Buenos dias, Irene. Coffee still good for after your classroom morning? I can do Tuesday at 11.
Tuesday works. I am keeping it simple this week; after the dentist and all that cooking in February, my little book scared me.
Ay, yes. One week plain meals, then coffee. Did the school line come in already?
Yes, 625 showed Wednesday. I wrote it beside the 2,500 plan so I do not pretend I have more than I do.
Irene, are you still coming to Bayland tomorrow? I saved you the lighter bat from last time.
Yes, but only one turn at first base and no running like I am 40. I already packed the wrap and the little ice bag.
Good. We can sit after and drink coffee. No showing off for those ladies, por favor.
I know. I did my slow park loop this morning, so tomorrow I will just enjoy the team.
Abuela, are we still going to the mall after art club?
Maybe just for your sketch pens. I left my blouse in the basket, I can fix the sleeve tonight.
The blue one? I can bring the tiny scissors from my kit.
Yes mija. Also remind me to use the black beans already soaking, no drive-thru after.
Abuela, I put the birthday pictures where Tia Ana tagged everybody. The one with your apron came out cute.
I saw mija. I only looked quick because I was checking the church fish fry post too.
Also I have to show you the 12-second video from lunch. You won't get it if I just send it lol.
Show me tomorrow after tamales. Tonight the phone goes away early.
Did you write your numbers today, hermana? No guessing.
Yes, 138 over 82 before breakfast. I put it in the little notebook.
Bueno. And take the new little pill with food like they told you.
I did. One thing at a time, right?
Ok Ma, I can stop by after the AC job. You still want me to look at that back room window?
Yes, just the latch. Please don't move the boxes in there; I have all the old statements stacked by year.
Got it. Ana asked if you ever thought about letting someone use that room since it's empty most weeks.
No mijo. I like my doors quiet, and I already have enough with the bank draft, water, gas, and insurance this month.
Irene, are you still coming Friday? The ladies asked if your soft triangle piece was for the table.
Yes, I will bring it after I tuck in the last threads. The station was playing Los Panchos and I got three more rows done.
Good. Bring it in a plain bag, not the nice one. Someone will be grateful, bendiciones.
Abuela can we come after church? Maya asked if the yellow blanket is still at your couch.
Yes mija, the yellow one and the blue one are clean. I put the little books back in the basket too.
She also said please the flat cheesy ones from the pan lol
I have masa ready. Tell your mom not to buy snacks on the way.
Abuela are you making the flat little ones this weekend? I can help press them
If I pass by the little place on Hillcroft for masa. Today I only did the H-E-B bag and the pharmacy window.
Ok I can bring cheese from our fridge if you want
Bring yourself, mija. I have beans soaking already.
Vas a hacer sopa hoy?
Si. I picked oregano from the pot and a little cilantro. No cube today.
Bueno. Those cubes make everything too strong anyway.
The leaves smell better. I am saving the tomatoes for tomorrow.
I put Tia Rosa's address and the hotel screenshot in the cousins chat. Look when you sit down.
I saw it. I moved a little money to the blue envelope after church, not much but steady.
Bueno. One thing at a time. Did Ana send the old picture from San Miguel?
Yes, in the same chat. I keep staring at Mama so young in that doorway.
Ok Ma, Lucia's birthday is at 6. Want me to bring anything besides plates?
Bring ice, mijo. I will just take a little from Marta's glass for the toast. That is enough for me.
Got it. Also I put the Treasury deposit date on your fridge calendar like you asked.
Thank you. I need that date before I pick up the refills at H-E-B.
Ma, thunder starting by my side. You already did your outside stuff?
Yes, I did Bayland before 7 and gave the hibiscus a little drink after lunch.
Ok Ma. Stay inside if it gets loud. I can pass tomorrow before work.
I am in already. The rest can wait until the light comes back in the morning.
Abuela, for my history board can I use the photo of Bisabuela with the blue dress?
Yes, but write her name correctly. She worked long days and still kept her hands gentle.
Can you help me with the Spanish caption tomorrow?
After I take Marta to the clinic. Bring your notebook, not only your phone.
Hermana, Father Cruz wants to do a misa for mami y papi this Saturday. 47 anios since papi came up from Santa Tecla, can you creer?
Ay Dios. Si, vamos. I'll bring the flores.
Also estoy thinking about your cumple. 76! You were the Houston baby and I was the recien llegada con mami en el avion lol
Don't remind me jaja. June 14 vendra rapido.
Ma, Ana said the cousins may all come Sunday after church. You want me to bring extra chairs?
Tell her not this Sunday, mijo. Last week I had my hour with Celia and that was enough running around for me.
Ok Ma. I can stop by alone and check the porch light instead.
That is better. You and me, quick visit, no crowd.
Mami, you left the laminated cards on my kitchen table. Are those for school?
Yes, please put them by the door. Ms. Lee needs the bathroom-step pictures before Friday morning.
Mija, did the water bill show paid on your screen? Mine says posted March 10 but I keep going back to it.
You even made two sets?
Yes, paid. I sent you the screenshot. Please don't log in again from that text link.
One for the wall and one for little hands. If it is not ready, the room gets loud.
Gracias. I wrote it in the notebook and I'm taking the yarn to Marta's later so my hands stay busy.
Good. Also ask CenterWell about the Friday appointment list if they have someone Spanish-speaking and low cost. I can call during my break if you want.
Mom, can the kids stay with you from 3:40 to 5:15? I got stuck covering front desk.
Bring them. I have fruit cut and some beans with rice from yesterday.
Perfect. Leo might ask for the dinosaur book again.
It is on the low shelf with crackers in the tin.
Buenos dias, Irene. Coffee still good for Saturday morning?
Yes, if my knees behave. I almost wrote a long note where the church ladies would all see it, then erased it.
Ay, better to breathe first. Did Marta settle you down last night?
Buenos dias, Irene. Did you see St. Matthew posted the Lent supper times? I sent it to you on the blue app in case the text picture is blurry.
She did. I told her the whole thing on the phone and slept better after.
Yes, I saw it this morning with Gloria's grandson photos. Better in daylight for me.
Good. At night everything looks bigger than it is. Close it and rest, amiga.
I saw the box you left by the hall. Same blue one from '88?
Yes. I only opened it because Celia needed dates. After that it goes back in the closet.
One thing at a time. You made a whole life after that box, hermana.
I had lesson plans to write and children waiting. Speaking of, I am taking soup to Ana before noon.
Irene, if lluvia keeps up, don't force St. Anne's tonight or Sunday. One thing at a time.
I know. I already told Rosa I can do the beans only if the knee is calm by Saturday.
Good. And bring Mama's candle back to me before you put the table away, okay?
Si, I wrapped it with the small cross and the old prayer cards.
Irene, did you find the tax paper from the clinic? One thing at a time.
Si. It was in the blue 2025 folder, behind the house insurance. I moved the new envelope to 2026 so I stop opening the same drawer.
Good. Put a clip on it, hermana. And eat something before you go chasing papers.
I wrote oatmeal already in the little book. The top page has today: call tax office, pay water, then only the things in my head under the line.
Ok Ma, I can come Tuesday for the porch rail. Morning or after lunch?
After lunch is easiest. The center keeps me 8:30 to 12:30 unless somebody is missing.
Good. Don't let them stretch you too much again.
I tell Rosa I can help once in a while, but I like coming home while the day is still young.
Buenos dias mi amiga. Que Dios te bendiga. Pensaste mas en lo de anoche? El comentario del senor sobre las camaras apagadas me dejo pensando.
Buenos dias Celia. Si, pense toda la noche. Las camaras estan ahi por una razon. Si las apagas a proposito, no deberias seguir con la placa.
De acuerdo. Y la mayoria hace su trabajo bien, es duro lo que hacen. Pero los pocos que abusan no pueden quedarse.
Exacto. Y tu y yo sabemos que no a todos los tratan igual en esos paros. Por eso voy a volver el mes que viene.
Good morning, Irene. Coffee Tuesday still? The place by the school has those cheese rolls you like.
Let's sit at my kitchen table this time. I have café, pan dulce in the freezer, and enough soup for two.
That sounds lovely. Should I bring anything?
Only your good eyes. I need you to tell me if the tan skirt seam is straight before I wear it again.
Abuela I put the nurse paper in your blue folder. It has the chart for grandparents too lol
Abuela can we do tamales when I come Saturday? I can help shred the chicken this time.
Good, mija. I will show it to Dr. Patel Monday before I do anything at Walgreens.
Maybe pupusas instead, mija. Last month the big family cooking pushed my pages too high, and I am trying to stay near 2,500 now.
Mom said use the .gov page, not random Facebook screenshots.
Yes, I know. The pharmacist also told me the same page to read.
Ok I can bring the cheese from mom's house lol. Do you still have to check the bank tomorrow?
Tomorrow I check the 2,050 line and then next Friday the school one again.
Abuela can I bring the mint candies from my backpack tomorrow? Everyone at school says they help sore knees lol
No, baby. I only use what the H-E-B lady says is okay with my bottles.
Ok ok. Mom said your cards are in the blue pouch by the coupons.
Yes, the blue pouch stays in my purse. Same counter every time, less confusion.
Mija, the parish bulletin says volunteers needed for the paper forms after Mass. You going?
Only one hour. Those forms scare people, and Mama always said someone helped Papi read his first stack.
Sí. And don't argue with Tía about the yard signs today.
I won't. I just tell her I read the names and watch who shows patience with families like ours.
I found the little notebook. Papa wrote numbers fine but made me read the work notices, remember?
I remember. He still knew every pipe, lock, and broken stair in those buildings.
Mama had me read the labels on thread envelopes. Her hands knew the rest.
Bring it Monday. Ana keeps asking what to put for me, but there is no campus card or papers from a base to copy.
Irene, did the tax office letter come? One thing at a time, hermana.
Yes. I put it with the county papers. Same little house, same forms, every March.
You have kept that place longer than some marriages, ay.
And every envelope still comes to me. I paid the county part and will do the bank one Monday.
Ok Ma, I left the cuff batteries on your kitchen table before work.
Thank you. The top number behaved better after I walked before breakfast, but my stomach was jumping while I waited.
Call me if it climbs again. And take the curb ramp by the park, not those cracked steps.
I did the flat side today. Slow and steady, then warm towel when I got home.
Ok Ma I saw your voicemail. You don't need to drive by city hall today.
I know. My knees and that many people, no. But I cannot stay quiet when they talk about teachers like they are the problem.
Send the email like Ana said. Safer.
I sent it. Also added the part about children hearing grownups call families names on television.
Ma, that blue bottle picture you sent has no doctor name on the page.
I thought so. The lady in the comments kept saying buy today.
Ok Ma. Don't order. Bring it to your appointment if you want to ask.
Good. I will just keep it in my notes.
Mami, the front desk gave me the vaccine form in English only. Can I send it before 10?
Send it. I will mark the lines you need and call you on your break.
Also Mateo stayed up crying about the spelling test.
Tell him I saved two pupusas. We will eat, then practice five words with no rushing.
Mom, did Salazar's office send the paper with the codes? I can look at it on my break.
They sent it. The big number is why I keep moving that appointment. The new lenses are waiting too.
Send me both screenshots. Sometimes they have a cash price or a monthly option if you ask before the visit.
I will. I paid extra on the card this morning, but the car and faucet are still sitting there.
Mom, the heat alert is showing again for this afternoon. Are you still going to H-E-B?
No, I did my little round by the park early. Now I am staying under the fan.
Good. Put the patio plants where they get shade, okay?
Already moved two pots and stood there a minute with the hose. That helped.
Buenos dias, Irene. Coffee today or is your house full of young shoes again?
Coffee next Saturday better. The front room still has blankets everywhere from Lucia, and Ana wants the blue bag back.
Next Saturday is fine. Rest your knees before everyone asks you for tamales.
Buenos dias, Irene. Coffee after church tomorrow, or are you still doing errands?
After church I need Fiesta for the dried chiles and whatever tomatoes are cheaper there.
Then coffee can wait until Tuesday. Take your list and don't tire your knee.
Good morning, Irene. Coffee Tuesday still works? I can help you read the flight page if the tiny print is bothering you.
Tuesday is better. I have to leave room for the refill on Monday.
Tuesday is good. I printed the page. The March price is high, so I am waiting before I touch that envelope.
Bring it with your glasses. Also send me the picture Ana posted yesterday; the one with all the aunts outside the church.
I will forward it from the green chat. Marta says half the cousins are still choosing dates.
Abuela, for my history project can I use that photo with everyone packed in the kitchen?
The one from the house near Fondren? Yes. Tia is half hidden by the pantry door.
Is that the radio on top of the fridge? The caption can say what was playing?
Say the morning news and the slow trio songs your great-grandpa liked while breakfast was starting.
Mana, you left lavender yarn on my chair. Is that the one for Tia Rosa?
Si, for her shoulders when the clinic rooms are cold. I made half the border last night with the little radio on.
She will use it. Don't make it too fancy, she saves everything like a treasure.
I know. I will wrap it in tissue, no box.
Ma, I can bring those bamboo sticks after the AC job.
Good, the peppers are leaning. Bring two if you have them.
Ok Ma. You still want limes too?
Yes, for the chicken with cilantro. It tastes fine without shaking extra on top.
Abuela can I record you doing the tin can song? The one you used with the little kids, not the church one lol
Only if you hold the phone steady. I need the slow part for my folder, where the children repeat the animal words.
Ok. Also the scary lady story? I can draw her but maybe not TOO scary for babies.
Make her gentle, mija. This page is for teachers to know what to change for the smallest ones.
Mom, send me the clinic statement when you get home. The adjustment line might be wrong.
I will. I circled $67.40 and put it with the tax notice. I don't like paying twice because I missed one line.
Good. Also don't pay the contractor deposit until Rafael looks at the unit.
Yes. I already told him I need the checking account to cover lights, food, and the policy draft first.
Ya acostada? You sounded tired earlier.
Almost. I found the chamomile box you like, and that detective book is finally getting good.
One thing at a time. If the pressure number is strange again, you call Ana or the doctor, okay?
Okay. I wrote the number down. For now I am doing the cup and one chapter, not making myself busy.
Mija, the pharmacy bottle says 10 now. Last year it was 5, right?
I checked the page you sent. The chart is from cdc.gov, last updated in February.
Yes, Dr. Patel changed it after those higher home numbers you showed him. Same time every morning.
Thank you. Dr. Patel's nurse said the same one is fine for my age.
Then ask Walgreens to print the after-care sheet too, just so you have it.
I will. I do better when the doctor and the pharmacist both explain it.
I keep checking Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday so I can show the page next visit.
Good. Send me a photo of the page before you go, just so the dates are clear.
Abuela, why do you have so many tiny handprints drying on your table?
Tomorrow we make a spring wall. I still need labels: red/rojo, sun/sol, leaf/hoja.
I can cut the leaf ones after homework. They are cute.
Gracias. Then I can finish the rhyme cards and the little counting cups before Friday.
Mom, Lucia's teacher asked if you still have the Spanish-English welcome sheet you used with parents. She wants to see how you worded it.
I have the clean copy. No need to tell her where the old draft came from.
Got it. Also, please let me order dinner if you are coming over after tutoring.
I already made rice and chicken. I will drop the sheet, feed everybody, and go home before the traffic gets bad.
Irene, bendiciones. Are we still meeting for coffee after your Thursday visit, or did the time change again?
Still 2:15. I checked the card, the phone reminder, and the paper on the fridge. Too many times.
Bring your blue scarf project and that little notebook. We can sit near the window like last time.
I may ask the front desk first about that woman from the parish flyer. Only if it is not expensive and I don't have to start from zero.
Ok Ma, Lucia says she sent you another clip and you asked where the sound button is.
Ay, that little video place moves too fast. She can show me Sunday.
Leave it for Sunday then. You already checked the reunion pictures?
Only the first few. I am closing the phone now before I start reading everything.
Mom, Lucia's art club has a fundraiser Saturday at 2. Marta may go too. Want me to add you?
No, hija. I already promised Celia I would look at those preschool papers with her later this month.
Got it. I will take pictures for you.
Thank you. Pictures are fine. I do better when the week has just the people I know.
Ma, el formulario del notario para el poder solo pide si te han fichado alguna vez. Marco no, verdad?
Marca no, mija. Nunca. Ni una multa de transito que pasara a algo mas.
Ok perfecto. Eso hace el papeleo facil. Lo firmamos el sabado cuando lleves los tamales?
Si. Y dile a Lucia que tambien necesito que me ayude con el correo del centro de Hiram Clarke, llego algo del comite.
Abuela can I use your printer for my civics handout? It's the school board one.
Yes baby. Print two. I want to compare who mentioned breakfast, nurses, and smaller rooms.
My teacher said look past the ads lol
Your teacher is right. We look at how they speak when nobody important is watching.
Marta, call me when you finish breakfast. The bank letter came and I need your calm voice.
I have toast now. Ten minutes.
And don't write about it on your page, ok? Too many metidos.
No, no. Just you. I'll answer when you ring.
Irene, ya comiste? You said you stayed late again.
I ate crackers. The 3-year-old room had a hard pickup, so we practiced what to say tomorrow.
One thing at a time. Do not carry the whole school in your purse.
Just the little script, the color labels, and my red pen. Then I am done.
Ana, Facebook showed me another one about sugar numbers. Can I send it before I mention it to your aunt?
Send it. If it has no clinic, no author, and a checkout page, leave it alone.
It has a red headline and four exclamation marks. I closed it.
Good call. I will text you the page from the diabetes association after breakfast.
Abuela, for my family poster can I draw Abuelo with a ladder and tool bucket?
Yes, and put the big ring of keys. He carried that everywhere.
For Abuela Ana said to draw the black Singer machine and folded dresses. Is that okay?
Perfect. For me just put my name and Houston, no cap-and-gown picture and no uniform picture.
Abuela my club is collecting picture books for Ms. Keller's class. Do you still have the doll box?
Yes, in the closet by the sewing basket. I washed the blue shirt one and the brown overalls one.
Ms. Keller said the little kids notice that stuff right away.
They do. After all the shouting on the news, I want your cousins to see kinder faces at school.
Hermana, one thing at a time. Did you call about the $1,000 estimate or only stare at the paper?
I called. If it stays around $400 I can cover it, but the $1,000 one has to be payments.
Bueno. Ask them to fix the painful part first and leave the extra polishing for later.
That's what I said. I still need the stronger lenses, so I can't empty the checking account.
Ma, I'm by Beechnut later. Want me to look for that old corner store you talked about?
It was closer to Chimney Rock, where your grandfather bought batteries for the radio.
Ok Ma. Was that before or after Tia stayed in the front room?
Same years. Marta and I had to keep our school shoes under the sofa then.
Ok Ma, I saw Ana's poll. July weekend is hard for me but I can make Saturday if you book early.
I am not booking yet. I put away $60 today and want to see if the fare drops.
Send me the link in the green app. I can check it after this AC call.
Sent. Also tell Lucia to add the candle photo for Tia Rosa before I forget.
abuela!! art club is doing a heritage month board, Ms. Alvarez asked what to put for me
Que linda mija. Pon Hispanic, Salvadoran American. Latina works too.
ok pegue una little flag de El Salvador next to abuelo's photo. she asked were u born there too?
No amor, yo naci aqui en Houston. Mis papas vinieron de alla. En la casa puro espanol, en la escuela puro ingles.
Ok Ma, I'm leaving my place in 20. Traffic on 59 looks ugly.
No rush. Lucia is finishing homework at the table and I packed your container.
Thanks. Ana said she can get the backpack from me tomorrow near her office.
Good, because the house will be too quiet tonight after all that music.
Mija, one thing at a time. Did you finish the papers from the county?

Bueno. Pay what is due, keep the rest quiet.
That's what I am doing. The roof patch can wait two weeks if the A/C behaves.
Ma, I can stop by after work. You still need copies of those pages?
Yes, 20 copies if it is not too much. The page with the morning song needs color, the budget page can be black and white.
Ok Ma. Is this for the lady asking about the small class near Bissonnet?
For her and for Celia to read. They asked how I keep the story short and still bring the families into it.
Mom, I can swing by the annex at 4:10 if you still want to go before the weekend crowd.
Yes, thank you. I just need five minutes to copy the last answers from the League pages onto my yellow sheet.
Take the Chronicle page too if it helps. I'll park near the side door.
I have it clipped with the church ladies' notes. I don't like guessing in the booth.
Mom, early voting is still open at the community center until 7. Do you need me to print the sample page?
No, I folded the one from the mail into my purse notebook. I marked the names after lunch.
Okay. Take your ID and the small card. Want me to call after work?
I have ID, card, and water by the door. When I come back I will put the sticker in the March page with the beans I soaked and the calls for tomorrow.
Ma, I saw your missed call. Everything okay?
Yes mija. Just awake. I made the little cup from the flower tin and opened the book Lucia left here.
Okay. If your stomach is still bothering you tomorrow, message Dr. Klein before lunch. I can help with the portal.
I will. Tonight I am only trying a few pages so my head stops counting things.
Buenas noches, Irene. I saved you the sign-up sheet for the nine evenings in December and two kitchen slots for April.
Thank you, Celia. Put me for one April morning, nothing with heavy pots.
Of course. Did you make it last Sunday, or did the cold keep you home?
I went, but Ana drove me and I left before lunch. My knee was talking.
Irene, vas manana con los ninitos or staying home?
Morning only, hermana. Rosa asked me to add Thursday because Nora is sick.
Ay, one thing at a time. You already gave them many years.
I know. I still like the children, just not every long day anymore.
Ma, can I stop by after lunch or are you at the center today?
At Room 3 until 12:45. Wednesday is circle rug, picture book, and counting buttons.
Ok Ma. I will come at 2. Need me to print those family notes?
Please print 12. Half say bring jacket, por favor; half say extra socks, please.
Mom, did the dental portal take the March payment?
Yes, confirmation came. I moved a little from the blue envelope and put the white sneakers back in the online cart.
Ok. Do you need groceries dropped off this weekend?
Not yet. I found two cans of tomatoes, rice, and the heel patches for my brown shoes.
Ma, el foco de atras ya lo cambie ayer. No quiero que te vuelvan a parar y te pongas asi.
Gracias mijo. Sabes que aunque no haya hecho nada, se me sube la presion cuando veo las luces atras.
Lo se. A Juan del taller le pasa igual y nunca ha tenido ni un problema tampoco. No eres tu sola.
Por eso voy a las reuniones del centro. Si las camaras se usan bien y revisan las quejas, va cambiando poco a poco para todos.
Ok Ma, we can stop by after soccer around 6. Kids will be hungry.
I saved chicken and rice, and I can warm tortillas with cheese fast.
Lucia asked if you still have the small blanket for the couch.
Yes, and the snack drawer is full. If they stay longer, I have masa left from the weekend.
Mom, I labeled the scan folder: Fondren house, kitchen table, school picture. Check if I got the years right.
Kitchen table is the year Tia was with us. Put Marta's name next to me, not behind the boys.
Got it. The little note on the back says 'radio loud, Mama cooking.'
That sounds right. Those songs filled the whole room before school.
Mom, Lucia said you had the Spanish station loud enough for the porch. Are you doing another yarn night?
Only the last rows. The green one is for the basket, and the pink one can go to Marta if it fits her.
Please keep one for yourself one day.
Maybe. These are already promised, mija.
Buenos dias amiga, Dios te bendiga. Quick favor - the principal at St. Anne's asked if I knew anyone who could talk to the 2nd graders for their unit on Central America.
Buenos dias Celia. Yo puedo. I'll tell them about growing up in southwest Houston, papas from El Salvador, pupusas on Sundays, todo eso.
Perfect, they will love it. She said any day before June 12. I told her you turn 76 two days later jeje
Jaja Celia! Si, June 14. Let's pick a Tuesday, my knee likes mornings.
Buenos dias, Irene. I put aside three board books and two soft dolls from my storage tub. Coffee Tuesday?
Tuesday is good. Thank you, Celia. I sent another $8 to the group helping parents find their children.
Ay, that story has stayed with you.
It has. And those little ones in class remember who gets shown and who gets left out.
Irene, coffee Monday still good? Bring your little notebook if you want me to help copy the dates neatly.
Yes, I checked this morning and Wednesday. The top one stayed under 140 both times.
That sounds calmer than when Dr. Patel changed your bottle last summer. Rest tonight, amiga.
I will. I already set tomorrow's tablet by the coffee cup.
Abuela can I sleep over tomorrow? I can bring my art stuff and not make a mess lol
Yes, bring the small bag. The front room is for sleeping only, no opening drawers or closet.
Ok ok. Mom said ask if you need help with those envelopes on the table.
Tell her I finished them: lights, water, insurance, and the little bank slip. Now I can make beans.
Lucia, your mama is busy. Can you help me find where this video came from? It says doctors hate this secret.
Abuela that phrase is everywhere lol. Send me the link, I can tap the profile.
I did not press the button. It wanted my card first.
Yeah no. I'll ask my mom later too, but don't put your card there.
Abuela I added the candle pic and the voice note from Tia Rosa to the big chat.
Thank you mija. Her voice made me cry a little. When I was your age those streets were only stories at the table.
Send me the place name again? I want to label the drawing right.
Abuela can I take pics of the little red tomatoes tomorrow? Art club needs texture photos
Abuela did you still go around the park today? It was windy.
Yes, but do not step near the mint. It is running everywhere.
Only twenty minutes by the benches. The tight feeling settled after I slowed my breathing and kept moving.
San Miguel, near the old church. Ask Ana for the photo with the blue doors too.
Lol okay. Are you making beans?
Good. Dad said no sprinting to beat your friends tomorrow lol.
Yes, with mint tea after and cilantro in the pot. Tell your mom I am not using the packet she brought.
Tell him I promised. Two innings sitting, one at first, then home with ice and soup.
Abuela, can we go to that park tomorrow when I come over?
Yes, but early, mija. By lunch the air feels too heavy.
Okayyy. I can help with your plant babies first lol
Good. We give them water, take a few slow breaths, then we go while the sun is still kind.
Irene, did H-E-B charge you the same as last month?
Almost. I waited until the 27th check landed, then paid $11 and $6. The pharmacist remembered to check both cards.
Good. One thing at a time. No borrowing Anita's stronger tablets, okay?
No, hermana. I asked first and took only the plain one from my cabinet after breakfast.
Ok Ma, I can pick up the folding chairs after work. You still watching the kids tonight?
Yes. Bring the chairs and the tire receipt. I made beans for you too.
Lucia says you told her to redo the poster title cleaner.
She has good hands. I want her to show that, and to know whose picture she is carrying.
How did your little notebook end, hermana? You sounded worried after the dentist bill.
Better. March is landing around 2,520 if I do not go back to Fiesta tomorrow.
Good. One thing at a time. The preschool money came twice this month, yes?
Yes, both Fridays showed. With the other regular line, the top of the page was 3,300 before anything got taken out.
Mom, do you still need me to order the sandals from the sale link?
Hold it for now. I used the envelope for H-E-B and my two prescriptions.
Ok. Want me to bring anything Tuesday?
Only if you pass Fiesta: one bag rice and the red cans, no rush.
Irene, before I forget, should we hold April 9 or April 10 for our usual place?
April 9 is better. Morning, please, before the stores get busy.
Then April 9 at 10. I will not invite Rosa; we can talk easier.
Thank you, Celia. I like when it stays simple like that.
